evidence: Cic. Caecin. 5: rēs aperta ac simplex (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Food, dress or speech with nothing added; also a matter with nothing tangled in it, rēs aperta ac simplex. Of a person, simplex is open and without guile (see direct). “It’s simple”, meaning “it’s easy”, is facile est (see easy).

terms.gloss: plain, modest, slender (of food, a table, a way of life)
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 3.49: tenuem vīctum antefert cōpiōsō (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: plain, frugal; of a person, thrifty and sensible
terms.comment: Properly a dative, “fit for food”, then “serviceable, honest, temperate”; as an adjective it never changes its ending (Lewis & Short, s.v. frūx).

phrases.latin: cibī simplicēs, agrestia pōma, recēns fera aut lac concrētum: sine apparātū, sine blandīmentīs expellunt famem
phrases.english: their food is simple: wild fruit, fresh game or curdled milk; they drive away hunger without fuss and without relishes

phrases.latin: potes apparātius cēnāre apud multōs, nusquam hilarius simplicius incautius
phrases.english: you can dine more grandly in many houses, but nowhere more merrily, simply and freely

phrases.latin: sī sine carne volēs jentācula sūmere frūgī, haec tibi Vestīnō dē grege massa venit
phrases.english: if you want a plain breakfast without meat, here is a cheese for you from a Vestine flock
